hints.title: Cooperative Coroutine Cancellation
hints.text: Controlling an asynchronous generator with cancellation support requires driving its step progression while listening for an external cancel signal.

hints.title: Driving Generator Steps with Throw Handling
hints.text: Await each yielded promise. If the cancel function is invoked before completion, inject an error into the generator via generator.throw("Cancelled") so it can run catch/finally blocks.

hints.title: Step Progression Blueprint
hints.text: Create promise with resolve/reject. Define step(nextFn, arg): try { res = nextFn(arg) } catch (err) { reject(err); return; } if (res.done) resolve(res.value); else Promise.resolve(res.value).then(v => step(() => generator.next(v)), e => step(() => generator.throw(e))). In cancel(): step(() => generator.throw("Cancelled")). Return [cancel, promise].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: S: number of generator yield steps
complexity.notes: Each yield step advances the coroutine asynchronously in constant memory.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simply rejecting the outer promise leaves the inner generator dangling without executing its finally cleanup blocks.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: generator.throw cleanly unwinds generator state according to standard language semantics.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly handling generator.throw to allow internal try/catch/finally execution.

solutions.approach: Async Coroutine Runner with Generator Throw Delegation
